title: Print Bench
sub: Designs made with Claude Code and the claude-3d-printing tools, in their print colours. Turn them, measure them, download them.
foot: Built with tools/print_bench.py from github.com/kalmehdar/claude-3d-printing. Grams are an estimate from the shape (1 mm walls, 15% infill), about 20% either way; your slicer's figure wins.

models.name: Rack status LED bar
models.for: A whole hardware project: 16 addressable LEDs and an ESP32-C3 on a board designed, routed and checked with Claude in KiCad, behind a printed 1U faceplate with a white diffuser window. Runs WLED. Shown as it prints, face down, with the board on its four standoffs above it.
models.status: Fit first: board not yet ordered; read hardware/led-bar/REVIEW.md
models.material: Faceplate PETG black, diffuser PETG white; the board is made by JLCPCB
models.credit: Designed with Claude: hardware/led-bar (circuit.py, layout.py, case.scad)

models.name: Four-colour test card
models.for: The first print on a new multi-head printer. Every colour borders every other colour once; if the edges stay crisp, purge and retraction are right.
models.material: PETG, four heads: red, blue, white, black

models.name: Colour-coded Gridfinity bins
models.for: Eleven bins that fill a 5 x 5 Gridfinity tray, 42 mm tall, each name printed into a band in its category colour: red power, blue network, white storage, plain black for the rest.
models.status: Ready: prints as two plates, because the set plus a four-colour prime tower overflows a 270 mm bed
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/gridfinity-bin.scad); Gridfinity is Zack Freedman's open standard

models.name: Clip-on cable tags
models.for: One tag per lead end, the colour saying what the lead carries and the ID printed in. Each clip is sized to its own cable, from mains down to slim Cat6: measure yours and set LEADS.
models.status: Fit first: print one tag per cable type and check it snaps on

models.name: Filament swatch card
models.for: One card per spool: its name and the temperatures it printed well at, printed in, plus a 0.4 to 1.6 mm step strip that shows how see-through the colour is. A hole takes a keyring.
models.status: Ready: set swatch_name, nozzle and bed for each spool
models.material: Two heads: the spool's colour, and a contrasting one for the text

models.name: Desk cable clip
models.for: Snaps over a cable and sticks to the desk edge with a 20 x 20 mm adhesive pad. Prints flat, no supports.
models.status: Fit first: set cable_d to your cable's diameter

models.name: Upgrade, before: a plain bin
models.for: Stands in for any STL you downloaded: one colour, no label, no magnets, and no source file to edit.

models.name: Upgrade, after: label, accent rim, magnets
models.for: The same STL upgraded by Claude without its source: M3 SCREWS printed into the front, the top 3 mm of the rim cut off and printed red, and 6 x 2 mm magnet pockets in the base. Turn it over to see the pockets.
models.material: PETG, three heads: black, red, white
models.credit: examples/models/upgrade-bin.scad: import() the STL, then difference, intersection and union
